# Fix `worklog_dir_flag` worktree resolution for worktrees under `<main>/.worklog/worktrees`

> **Provenance:** transferred from `CG-0MVZKL4WB000JPZT` (Tableau-Card-Engine
> store) by producer decision, where it was `discovered-from:CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY`
> (TCE worktree `wl-CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY-retire-legacy-choice-fields-and-the-clar`,
> commit `4975f6ff`), observed while running
> `render_report.py CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY` from that worktree. The CG item is
> deleted after transfer; the full intake brief lives here.

## Problem statement

`shared/status_lifecycle._detect_worklog_dir()` builds ancestor candidates as
`parent / ".worklog"` for **every** parent, so when the cwd sits inside
`<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` the ancestor `<main>/.worklog`
itself yields `<main>/.worklog/.worklog`; it also accepts any `.worklog`
directory **without** checking that it is initialised. Both defects make
`worklog_dir_flag()` hand `wl` a store root that is either non-existent
(no-op flag) or uninitialised (`wl` fails with
`"Worklog system is not initialized"`), so skill scripts that shell out to
`wl` break when run from an `implement.py` worktree.

## Users

- **AI agent running skill scripts from an implement worktree** — `/skill:report`,
  `/skill:audit`, `persist_audit.py`, and status/lifecycle helpers all resolve
  the store through `worklog_dir_flag()` / `resolve_worklog_flags()`.
  Story: *As an agent finishing work in a worktree, `render_report.py <id>`
  must read the main checkout's worklog so my report is populated and my
  status transition is written to the store the producer reads.*
- **Producer / operator** — needs a trustworthy store resolution so a run from
  a worktree cannot silently target a wrong or uninitialised store.
  Story: *As the producer, when an agent reports from a worktree, the item it
  reports on must be the item in the main checkout's store, with no manual
  `--worklog-dir` correction.*
- **Skill maintainer** — needs the resolution rule pinned by tests.
  Story: *As a skill maintainer, I need a regression test for the
  `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/…` layout so a future refactor of the ancestor
  walk cannot reintroduce a nested `.worklog/.worklog` path.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — worktree root resolves to the main checkout store.**
      With cwd = `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` and no `.worklog`
      in the worktree, `worklog_dir_flag()` returns
      `["--worklog-dir", "<main>/.worklog"]` (the initialised store), including
      when a stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` directory exists.
- [ ] **AC2 — no double suffix.** An ancestor directory already named
      `.worklog` is never extended to `.worklog/.worklog`; the worklog
      directory that is itself an ancestor is the candidate.
- [ ] **AC3 — initialised candidates only.** A candidate `.worklog` that is not
      initialised (`_is_initialized_worklog()` false — e.g. a worktree's
      committed `config.yaml`-only copy) is never returned; resolution
      continues to the nearest initialised ancestor, and returns `[]` (no flag)
      rather than an uninitialised path when nothing initialised exists.
- [ ] **AC4 — unit tests cover the worktree layouts.** New hermetic tests
      (tmp_path fixtures, no real `git worktree`, no network) covering:
      (a) `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` with a stale
      `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` present;
      (b) a **subdirectory** of a worktree whose committed `.worklog/` holds
      only `config.yaml` (the uninitialised-candidate case);
      (c) a plain nested project cwd (no `.worklog` between cwd and the project
      root) still resolving as today (no regression).
- [ ] **AC5 — existing precedence preserved, no weakening.** Precedence
      `explicit --worklog-dir` > prefix-to-sibling scan > cwd chain > no flag is
      unchanged, and the existing tests in
      `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` pass without
      edits to their assertions.
- [ ] **AC6 — documentation.** The resolution rule (initialised-only, no
      `.worklog/.worklog` nesting, worktree-ancestor special case) is stated in
      the code docstrings of `_detect_worklog_dir()` / `worklog_dir_flag()` and
      in `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (the section that says
      `StatusLifecycle` resolves the worklog dir automatically) and
      `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` (the worklog-store resolution note).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Fix lands in this repository.** The defective code is
  `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` here; `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to
  `skill/`. Do **not** edit another project's `.pi/`, and do not create a
  vendored copy of the helper.
- **Shared seam.** `status_lifecycle` is imported by every skill; keep the
  change narrow (one candidate-selection helper reused by both
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` and `worklog_dir_flag()`), with no behaviour change
  for cwds that already resolve correctly.
- **Fail closed, never guess.** Returning no `--worklog-dir` (so `wl` reports
  the real error) is preferred over returning a path that is not an initialised
  store.
- **Hermetic tests.** No real `git worktree`/network in the unit tests;
  `unittest.mock.patch` on `Path.cwd`-derived inputs or `tmp_path` layouts,
  matching the existing test module's style.
- **Gate order.** build → test → commit, never reversed; no ad-hoc `pytest` —
  run tests through the test skill (`/skill:test` / `run_tests.py`).

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- Source of truth: `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (this repo).
- `_detect_worklog_dir()` (line ~258) order: `<cwd>/.worklog` →
  `<git toplevel>/.worklog` → `for parent in cwd.parents: parent/".worklog"`;
  the last two gates call `is_dir()` only, never `_is_initialized_worklog()`.
- `worklog_dir_flag()` (line ~391) has a **second, different** ancestor walk
  that *does* check `_is_initialized_worklog()`, then falls back to
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` — so the two walks disagree.
- Reproduced (Tableau-Card-Engine checkout, registered worktree, git toplevel =
  the worktree):
  ```
  cwd=/home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>   (historical reproduction in a sibling project)
  _detect_worklog_dir() -> /home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/.worklog
  worklog_dir_flag()    -> ['--worklog-dir', '…/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/.worklog']
  ```
  The stale `…/.worklog/.worklog/` exists and contains only a `worktrees/`
  subdirectory (no `initialized` marker, no `worklog.db`).
- Reproduced (this repository, registered worktree, run from a **subdirectory**
  so the `cwd/.worklog` branch is skipped):
  ```
  cwd=…/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>/skill
  _detect_worklog_dir() -> <that worktree>/.worklog      # config.yaml only — NOT initialised
  worklog_dir_flag()    -> ['--worklog-dir', '<worktree>/.worklog']
  ```
  i.e. a second manifestation of the same defect (uninitialised candidate),
  at the worktree **root** even though the initialised main store is a direct
  ancestor. Both are in scope via AC1–AC3.
- `_resolve_repo_root()` already handles the worktree case for the framework
  root (`skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py::TestFrameworkRootDerivation`)
  — the framework root is correct; only the *store* resolution is wrong.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` covers prefix scan,
  `resolve_worklog_dir`, `resolve_worklog_flags` precedence and `run_wl`
  injection, but has **no** ancestor-walk / worktree-layout test.
- `skill/shared/worklog_sync.py` re-uses `worklog_dir_flag()`, so it is fixed
  transitively. `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` resolves its own target
  project root and is unaffected.
- Adjacent same-class defect, **filed separately** by producer decision as
  `SA-0MW0JI376007RON7` (see *Related work*):
  `skill/shared/code_freeze.py::_detect_worklog_dir()` (line
  ~48) duplicates the ancestor walk with the same `parent/".worklog"`
  construction and no initialisation check, so `code_freeze_marker_path()`
  would read `<main>/.worklog/.worklog/code-freeze.json` from a worktree.

## Desired change

1. Introduce one candidate-selection helper used by both
   `_detect_worklog_dir()` and `worklog_dir_flag()`:
   - for each ancestor, if the ancestor **is** a worklog directory
     (`name == ".worklog"`), the candidate is that ancestor itself; otherwise
     the candidate is `ancestor / ".worklog"`;
   - only accept a candidate when `_is_initialized_worklog(candidate)` is true
     (in the `_detect_worklog_dir` gate; `worklog_dir_flag` keeps its existing
     "no flag" contract when nothing initialised is found).
2. Delete the duplicated walk in `worklog_dir_flag()` in favour of the shared
   helper (no second, divergent rule).
3. Tests per AC4, in the existing
   `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` module style.
4. Doc updates per AC6.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — `_detect_worklog_dir()` (~line 258)
  gains the `.worklog`-named-ancestor rule and the `_is_initialized_worklog()`
  gate; `worklog_dir_flag()` (~line 391) re-uses the same helper instead of its
  own walk; docstrings per AC6.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` — new
  `TestWorklogDirAncestorWalk` class with the AC4 cases.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — the "`StatusLifecycle` resolves the same
  directory automatically" paragraph (~lines 84–88) gains the initialised-only /
  no-nesting rule.
- `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` — worklog-store resolution note
  (~lines 360–364).

## Related work

- `SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL` (open, intake_complete) — *implement.py finish reports
  status changes that the main worklog store does not show*. Same seam, wider
  scope (finish must pass an explicit store). Its "Existing state" note claims
  `worklog_dir_flag` "does resolve the main checkout store from a worktree";
  the evidence above shows that holds only when no stale
  `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` exists — this item carries the counter-example.
  Partial overlap only, so **not** a duplicate.
- `SA-0MW0JI376007RON7` — `code_freeze.py` resolves a worktree's
  non-initialised `.worklog` (the same walk duplicated in `code_freeze.py`).
  Filed separately by producer decision (Appendix Q2) and **blocked by** this
  item, so the shared rule lands first.
- `CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY` (Tableau-Card-Engine) — original discovery work item.
- `CG-0MUC5GVCJ0062BN7` (Tableau-Card-Engine, completed) — earlier
  worktree-resolution defect (`.pi/test-config.json` unseen from a worktree):
  same failure family, different file.
- `SA-0MSG57UNY009DE51`, `SA-0MSGH55OJ003WKYZ`, `SA-0MTOMCML900254CI`
  (completed) — the prefix-to-sibling seam and cwd-independence lineage this
  item extends.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: resolver regression elsewhere.** Other skills rely on
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` returning a non-initialised directory in exotic
  layouts. Mitigation: AC5 requires the existing suite to pass unchanged; the
  change only *narrows* accepted candidates, and `worklog_dir_flag()` keeps its
  "no flag" fallback so `wl` still reports its own error.
- **Risk: `.worklog`-named ancestor inside a normal project** (e.g. a directory
  literally called `.worklog` used for something else). Mitigation: the
  `.worklog`-named ancestor is only accepted when `_is_initialized_worklog()`
  is true.
- **Risk: styling split between the two walks** if only one is fixed.
  Mitigation: single shared helper (Desired change 1–2).
- **Scope-creep risk: fixing `code_freeze.py` in the same change.** Excluded by
  producer decision (Appendix Q2) — it is filed separately.
- **Assumption:** the "stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog`" directory is a local
  artefact (from an old run) and is not committed anywhere; the fix must not
  depend on its removal, because the nesting rule is wrong regardless.
- **Assumption:** unit tests can express the layout with `tmp_path` +
  `mock.patch` rather than creating real git worktrees (the existing module
  already models the framework-root worktree layout this way).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Where should the fix and its record land?** The defective code lives
  in SorraAgents (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`); the TCE checkout has no
  `skill/` tree, so a TCE `implement.py` worktree could not carry the change
  (the TCE-side `implement.py finish` fails closed on out-of-worktree edits).
  Options were: (a) transfer the item to the SA store; (b) create an SA item
  carrying code + tests, keep the CG item as a linked discovery record;
  (c) commit to SorraAgents `dev` from outside a worktree (breaks
  worktree-isolation). Agent recommendation: (b).
  **Answer (producer):** *"SA create there then delete this item"* — create the
  SA item with the full brief (this item) **and delete** the CG item, i.e. a
  transfer rather than a linked pair. Source: operator reply in the intake
  session `herdr-1793666897-1472625-2858`.
- **Q2 — Fold in the adjacent `code_freeze.py` defect?** Options: (a) fix both
  in this change via one shared helper; (b) keep this item narrow and file the
  `code_freeze` fix as a separate `discovered-from` item. Agent recommendation:
  (b).
  **Answer (producer):** *"file separately"* — the `code_freeze.py`
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` duplicate-walk fix is filed as its own item; this item
  stays narrow. Source: operator reply in the intake session
  `herdr-1793666897-1472625-2858`.
- **Q3 — Duplicate-work check (agent-resolved).** Searched both stores
  (`worklog_dir_flag`, `worktree resolution`, `nested worklog dir`) —
  `SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL` is the only overlapping item and its ACs do not cover
  the nesting/initialisation defects, so no duplicate close or rewrite was
  applied; it is cross-referenced in *Related work*. Answer: **no full
  duplicate; partial overlap cross-linked.**
## Impact

Skill scripts that shell out to `wl` (render_report, persist_audit, audit, status/lifecycle helpers) now resolve the main checkout's initialised worklog store correctly from any `implement.py` worktree cwd — `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/…`, its subdirectories, or a plain nested project — so an agent reporting or transitioning status from a worktree always targets the store the producer reads, with no manual `--worklog-dir` correction and no "Worklog system is not initialized" failure or `.worklog/.worklog` mis-targeting.

## Summary

Nothing ever re-checks a linter-derived work item against the current tree. Once filed, a refactor or audit finding stays open until a human or agent happens to look at it — even when the target file has been deleted or the diagnostic has not fired for weeks.

During the 2026-11-08 backlog review this was measured directly, and every sampled family was stale.

## Evidence

**115 open refactor items whose titled path no longer resolves or whose diagnostic no longer reproduces:**

| Class | Items | Verification |
|---|---|---|
| Target file deleted from the repo (`skill/proxy-usage-analysis/**`, a removed skill) | 37 | path does not exist |
| Target file exists, diagnostic no longer fires | 78 | `ruff check --isolated --select <RULE> <path>` → 0 hits in all 34 (path, rule) groups |

**73 open audit-side items** of the form `ruff <RULE> in <path> — candidate false positive` (`audit_runner.py` `FP_CANDIDATE_ANNOTATION`, created as "producer decision required" chores): **0 of 19 (path, rule) groups still fire** on the current tree.

Concrete examples of no-longer-reproducing findings that remained open:
- `S112` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — 22 items, 0 hits now.
- `SIM117` in `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_from_worktree.py` — 10 items, 0 hits now.
- `ISC004` in `tests/test_assignee_release_all_skills.py` — 7 items, 0 hits now.
- `PYI034`/`PYI036` in `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — 4 items, 0 hits now (these were orphaned children too).

Some of these block audits rather than sitting idle, so stale findings are not merely noise: `SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42` records the audit-side variant where every medium/low candidate-false-positive chore sets `needsProducerReview` and blocks closure.

## Why it matters

Stale items are indistinguishable from live work in every view. `wl next` will dispatch them, an agent will implement, and the audit skill must then decide whether a finding that no longer reproduces has been "fixed". The backlog reads as 444 actionable items when a large share are already resolved.

## Required behaviour (acceptance criteria)

1. Every linter-derived item records, at creation, the **exact verification command** and a **content fingerprint** (file hash + rule set) that produced it.
2. A re-verification sweep re-runs that command and, per item, classifies it as `still-reproduces`, `no-longer-reproduces` or `target-gone`, recording the evidence in a comment.
3. Items classified `target-gone` are closed with a rationale (or flagged for deletion), and items classified `no-longer-reproduces` are closed with the evidence comment — **never silently**.
4. The sweep is **dry-run by default** and only ever touches items it can attribute to a linter family (`Refactor` tag, `[SEVERITY] <path>` titles, `ruff <RULE> in <path>` titles). It must never close a human-authored bug or feature.
5. The sweep is runnable both ad hoc and as a scheduled/gated step (e.g. from the refactor skill or a `wl doctor`-style hook), and is idempotent.
6. Tests: target deleted → `target-gone`; diagnostic fixed → `no-longer-reproduces`; diagnostic still firing → untouched; human-authored item → never touched; dry-run makes no writes.

## Scope note

The sweep itself belongs in this repository (`skill/refactor/`, and the audit side in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`). If a worklog-level hook is preferred, that part belongs to the Worklog CLI project (`WL → /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`) and should be raised there — recorded as an assumption, not a decision.

## Key Files

- `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — record the verification command and content fingerprint (file hash + rule set) on every linter-derived item at creation (AC1).
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — record the same metadata for audit-side candidate-false-positive chores (`FP_CANDIDATE_ANNOTATION` creations); note the existing `CFP-Chore-Key:` marker is reused as a stable key in the sweep's attribution logic.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/reverify.py` (new) — the dry-run-by-default re-verification sweep: classify `Refactor`-tagged, `[SEVERITY] <path>`/`ruff <RULE> in <path>` items as `still-reproduces` / `no-longer-reproduces` / `target-gone`, comment evidence, close with rationale (AC2–AC5).
- `skill/refactor/tests/` + `skill/audit/tests/` — coverage for AC6 scenarios (target deleted, diagnostic fixed, still firing, human-authored untouched, dry-run no-writes).

## Impact

Stale, already-fixed findings stop inflating the backlog and stop being dispatched to agents, so the queue can be trusted to mean "work that still needs doing".

### Related work items
- **SA-0MQPP6TFJ008LU1N** – wl close: add recovery path for done parent with open children (completed)
- **SA-0MQFXG76T000A3LR** – wl delete should recursively delete child work items (completed)

# Intake Brief: Ship skill triggered audits should not mark for producer review

## Problem statement

When the ship skill's release gates auto-remediate a missing/stale/transient
audit by re-running `audit_runner.py issue <id> --strict`, that run follows the
**independent audit** contract and can write `--needs-producer-review yes`: a
top-level 'Ready to close: Yes' verdict that needs a producer decision, or an
independent top-level 'No' verdict, both arm the producer-review hold. These
are release-automation verification runs, not independent reviews, so the
release silently self-inflicts producer-review holds that block its own gates
(exit 9 producer-review gate, exit 12 final-validation sweep) and flood the
producer queue with items the release itself just touched. The audit behaviour
when run independently must stay exactly as it is today.

## Users

- **Producers running a release** — user story: "When I run `/skill:ship`, the
  release's own audit remediation must not set `needsProducerReview` on the
  items it re-audits — I don't want the release to block itself or queue
  spurious producer approvals I then have to clear."
- **Audit operators** — user story: "I want a ship-triggered re-audit to be
  distinguishable from an independent review: it verifies, it never queues
  producer attention; an independent audit still flags exactly as documented."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Ship-triggered runs leave the flag untouched.** When the ship skill's
   release gates (Step 2 audit readiness gate, Step 6 final-validation sweep)
   or its pre-flight `--refresh-audits` re-audit an item via
   `audit_runner.py issue <id> --strict` with a ship-trigger marker, the runner
   never writes `--needs-producer-review` — a top-level 'Yes' verdict that would
   otherwise require a producer decision leaves `needsProducerReview` untouched,
   and a top-level 'No' verdict also leaves it untouched (neither
   set nor cleared).
2. **Independent audit behaviour is unchanged.** An audit run without the ship
   marker behaves exactly as today: a top-level 'Yes' with a producer decision
   required still writes `--needs-producer-review yes` (subject to the
   preserved/untouched carve-outs of SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST and
   SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42), and an independent top-level 'No' still flags the item.
3. **Only the flag write is suppressed.** All other lifecycle behaviour of a
   ship-triggered run is unchanged: 'Yes' still advances to
   `completed`/`in_review`; 'No' still demotes to `open`/`plan_complete` (and
   stays subject to cascade-demotion suppression); the persisted report still
   records the verdict and a `Producer review: untouched (…)` metadata line.
4. **Targeted tests.** Tests exercise production code (not re-implementations)
   and lock: ship-triggered 'Yes' (top-level) → no `--needs-producer-review`
   write; ship-triggered 'No' (top-level) → no flag write, demotion still
   applied; marker absence → independent 'Yes'/'No' writes the flag exactly as
   today; the marker cannot leak (a run without it never suppresses).
5. **Documentation updated.** `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (producer-review rules),
   `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (Producer-review flag lifecycle) and
   `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` (audit-gate remediation
   sections) document that ship-triggered audits leave `needsProducerReview`
   untouched, and that surfaced manual remediation commands (operator-invoked)
   remain independent.
6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Impact

Producers no longer see a release's own audit remediation queue spurious
producer-review holds that block that same release, so `/skill:ship` no longer
self-blocks or forces manual flag clearing after every release.

## Constraints

- **Independent runs untouched:** the marker must only ever be set by
  ship-automated invocations; operator-invoked commands (the surfaced

  independent flagging behaviour.
- **No new flag-clearing behaviour:** the runner never writes
  `--needs-producer-review no`; ship-triggered suppression means "don't write
  the flag at all", not "clear it afterwards". The ship close step's authorised

- **No leakage risk from the mechanism:** the chosen trigger marker must not be
  accidentally set in an operator's shell, or every audit on that host would
  silently suppress producer flagging.
- **Verdict semantics unchanged:** suppression is about the producer-review
  flag only; 'Ready to close' conclusions, freshness, and gate blocking are

- **Repository boundary:** this repo (SorraAgents) owns both skills; no herdr/

  leak the same way. Recommend CLI flag (see Appendix Q1).

  report gains a new `untouched` reason; existing consumers must tolerate it

  existing `AUDIT_CASCADE_AUDIT` pattern; (c) ship clears the flag after each
  remediation run. **Recommended (Map, intake): (a) — explicit and leakage-safe;
  an env var can silently taint every audit on the host if set in a shell
  profile, and option (c) fights the runner's never-clear contract.** Source:

  `_resolve_producer_review_decision`, and `skill/ship/scripts/*.js`
  `runAuditCommand` defaults. Not producer-confirmed.
- **OPEN QUESTION ('No' verdict scope):** For a ship-triggered re-audit whose
  verdict is 'Ready to close: No', should the item still be demoted to
  `open`/`plan_complete` (only the flag suppressed), or should the demotion be
  suppressed too (behaving like the cascade-demotion carve-out for already
  `in_review`/`done` items)? **Recommended (Map, intake): keep the demotion,
  suppress only the flag — the item genuinely failed, so it must leave the
  release queue; the release gate already blocks on the failing verdict (exit
  12), and AC3/AC1 wording limits the change to the flag.** Source:
  `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` 'No' branch. Not producer-confirmed.
- **OPEN QUESTION (manual/operator runs):** The release gate output surfaces
  marker-free `python3 … audit_runner.py issue <id> --strict [--force]` and
  `batch --strict` hints for the operator to run manually. Should those
  operator-invoked runs also be treated as ship-triggered? **Recommended (Map,

  release-automation invocation sites get the marker (the seed context states

  now").** Source: check-audit-gate.js hint builders (~lines 404/536/656) and

# Intake Brief — More conversational standup reports (SA-0MWBRJ3KI006XJ46)

**Headline:** Add a second, conversational-polish iteration to the standup
skill's agent rendering workflow so the daily standup reads as natural prose —
free of "Title — description" bullets and repeated clause templates — instead
of a list of tasks.

## Problem statement

Daily standup reports still read as lists of tasks. The ContextHub report for
2026-11-13 is a bullet list of "Title — description" items, and other
projects' reports repeat the same clause templates sentence after sentence.
The pipeline's only LLM processing is the invoking agent's single rendering
pass over the structured JSON per `skill/standup/SKILL.md`; there is no second
pass that catches and fixes list-like or template-repetitive phrasing before
the report is written to `standups/` and committed.

## Users

- **The operator** who reads or listens to daily standups across projects
  (SorraAgents, AI_Hell, ContextHub, Tableau-Card-Engine, games_curator).
- **TTS listeners** who hear the report read aloud — bullet-style "Title —
  description" lines and repeated clause templates sound robotic.

### User stories

- As an operator, I want the daily standup to read as conversational prose so
  I can listen to it rather than scan it.
- As a TTS listener, I want the report free of "Title — description" bullets
  and repeated clause patterns so it sounds like natural speech.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/standup/SKILL.md`'s Report Rendering section documents a second LLM
   processing iteration — a conversational-polish pass: after the first
   clustered draft, the agent re-reads its draft and rewrites it so no line
   reads as a "Title — description" bullet and no clause template repeats
   across sentences, before persisting the report.
2. The polish pass is agent-side only: `generate_standup.py` remains a
   deterministic data layer with no LLM calls (architecture per
   SA-0MW6EUVGM009RMD2); no script code or script tests change.
3. The polish pass preserves the existing hard constraints: one sentence per
   item, the item's `## Impact` sentence used when present (else the
   `Title — user story` fallback content, re-phrased into flowing prose rather
   than em-dash template lines), per-section clustering, no work item IDs,
   first person, TTS-friendly dates, and the ~2-minute read budget.
4. The skill-document contract is pinned by a test (extend
   `skill/standup/tests/test_skill_md_clustered_report.py` or add a sibling
   test following the same pattern): SKILL.md describes the second-iteration
   step and the worked example contains no "Title — description" bullet lines
   or standup-specific repeated clause templates.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
   (`skill/standup/README.md` and `skill/standup/SKILL.md`).

## Constraints

- No changes to `generate_standup.py` or its tests — the script stays the
  deterministic data layer (SA-0MW6EUVGM009RMD2); the report narrative lives
  in the agent's rendering instructions.
- Dated standup history (`standups/*.md`) is never re-rendered; only the
  skill and its tests change.
- The change must reach every project via the global skill install
  (`scripts/install_pi.sh` refreshes `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup`); no per
  project copy to maintain.

## Existing state

- `skill/standup/SKILL.md` § Report Rendering (updated in SA-0MW6EUVGM009RMD2,
  pinned by `test_skill_md_clustered_report.py`): the agent clusters
  `--json` data into free-form categories, one paragraph per category, one
  sentence per item, no bullets — a single rendering pass with no self-review
  iteration.
- Evidence of the problem: ContextHub `standups/2026_11_13.md` (bullet list),
  SorraAgents `standups/2026_11_11.md` and AI_Hell `standups/2026_11_14.md`
  (repeated "On \<category\>," / "I am also…" openers and similar clause
  templates).
- Scheduled-prompt entry `{ id: "/skill:standup", intervalDays: 1, time:
  "06:05" }` in each project's `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` — every
  project consumes the same shared skill.

## Desired change

- Add a dedicated second iteration to the SKILL.md rendering workflow: after
  drafting the clustered report, the agent performs a conversational-polish
  pass that (a) rewrites any "Title — description" / "Title — user story"
  bullet-style lines into flowing prose, (b) removes repeated clause
  templates across sentences, and (c) re-verifies the grouped-paragraph
  render mode — then persists and commits the report as today.

## Key Files

- `skill/standup/SKILL.md` — add the second-iteration (conversational-polish)
  step to the Report Rendering section, before persisting.
- `skill/standup/tests/test_skill_md_clustered_report.py` — extend to pin the
  new contract (or add a sibling `test_skill_md_conversational_polish.py`
  following the same pattern).
- `skill/standup/README.md` — update if it describes the rendering workflow.

## Related work

- SA-0MW6EUVGM009RMD2 (completed) — update standup SKILL.md for agent-rendered
  clustered report; established the clustering contract this item builds on.
- SA-0MTWO7HFW001N9QJ (completed) — add project title to standup report
  template; established the `## <project_name> Standup Report` header.
- SA-0MWHZ7MD6007R07Z (open) — standup skill post-step: auto-publish standup
  podcast; different scope (publishing, not prose quality).
- WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 (herdr selection list) — source of truth for item
  selection; unaffected by this change.

## Risks & assumptions

- The polish pass is prose guidance for an LLM agent, so output quality varies
  by model and interpretation; the pinning test checks the documented
  contract, not generated prose (accepted — the render is agent-authored by
  design, per SA-0MW6EUVGM009RMD2).
- Re-phrasing the `Title — user story` fallback must keep the item's title
  and the user-visible value; the listener still needs to know *what* the
  item is.
- Assumed scope: only `skill/standup/` in this repo changes; dated standup
  history is never re-rendered; no per-project skill copies to maintain.
- Scope-creep guard: opportunities that surface (e.g. varying sentence
  openers, per-project voice) are recorded as linked work items, not folded
  into this change.

## Impact

Daily standup reports read as conversational prose rather than a task list —
no "Title — description" bullets and no repeated clause templates — so they
are pleasant to listen to and skim.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where should the 'second LLM iteration' live? A) Agent-side second
  pass in SKILL.md (recommended — fits the agent-render architecture now in
  place, applies to all projects immediately, no new infra); B) Script-side
  LLM refinement step/flag in `generate_standup.py` (reverses the
  deterministic data-layer design; adds cost/latency to the 06:05 run);
  C) Deterministic `*_tts` template phrasing tweaks only (cheapest; cannot
  fix whole-report repetition)." — Answer (producer): **A — agent-side second
  pass in SKILL.md**. Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-16 (comment
  SA-C0MWJCXC6P006LO3T).
- Q2: "What does 'less repetitive' primarily target? A) Vary sentence openers
  across the report (stop every line starting with 'On \<category\>,' /
  'I am also…'); B) Eliminate the 'Title — description' bullets and repeated
  clause templates (ContextHub-style); C) Both A and B (recommended — the
  second-pass iteration also re-verifies the clustered-paragraph render
  mode); D) Other (freeform)." — Answer (producer): **B — eliminate the
  "Title — description" bullets and repeated clause templates (ContextHub
  style)**. Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-16. Research: the ContextHub
  `standups/2026_11_13.md` report is entirely bullet lines of
  "Title — description" form; `test_skill_md_clustered_report.py` already
  forbids bullets, so the second pass re-verifies and also de-templates the
  `Title — user story` fallback phrasing. Note: Q2 chose B over the
  recommended C; opener variation ("On X," patterns) is intentionally out of
  scope.

# Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6)

## Problem statement

Implement sessions that run concurrently spend the overwhelming majority of their
wall-clock waiting on a single per-repository `flock`, because `implement.py finish`
holds that lock across its **whole** commit → fast-forward → push → post-push window
and the dev-push **pre-push hook runs the full test suite (~5.4 min)** inside it.
Every concurrent `finish` therefore serialises its expensive test run behind the
others. At the intended fan-out of **up to 6 concurrent sessions**, the sixth finish
queues behind five ~5-min full-suite runs.

## Evidence (2026-11-13, AI_Hell implement-skill sessions)

Analysed the 36 worktree sessions that started with the implement skill
(`~/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-AI_Hell-.worklog-*`):

- **668 min** summed session time over a **388 min (6.5 h)** wall-clock span —
  only **1.7x effective parallelism** at a **peak measured concurrency of 4**.
- **88–93%** of each long session's wall-clock was inside `bash` tool calls
  (waiting on processes), not model reasoning or edits.
- Time buckets: **wait_for_job 249 min (37%)** (215.9 min of it lock-waits),
  own `finish` 133 min (20%), scoped tests 57 min (9%), hand-rolled
  `sleep`/`grep` polling loops 48 min (7%).
- **57** "another run holds the repository lock" refusals; **46** observed
  lock-waits averaging **4.3 min** (median 5 min, **max 21.5 min**). Worst single
  tool call: **45 min** = a `for attempt in 1..8` retry loop absorbing five
  consecutive lock holders.
- **21** non-fast-forward rebase events, each creating a new tree that re-triggers
  the full-suite pre-push gate (9 full-suite gate runs today).
- 9 sessions were **no-ops** (3 messages, ~50 s) — drive retries that immediately
  gave up.

## Users

- **Operator** running a fan-out batch of up to 6 concurrent implement sessions
  (the intended operating point) on a single repository.
- **Implement-skill sessions** (leaf and driven child) whose `finish` currently queues
  behind other sessions' full-suite runs.
- **Producers/reviewers** who need the speed-up evidenced, not asserted.

User stories:

- As an operator running up to 6 concurrent implement sessions, I want `finish` to
  complete in minutes of real work rather than tens of minutes of serialised queueing
  behind other sessions' full-suite runs, so a fan-out batch finishes in roughly the

roughly the time of one work item, instead of waiting for six serialised five-minute

## Problem

When `implement.py drive` spawns a child session that dies before writing
anything (e.g. a transient provider error — `Provider finish_reason: error`),
the child is left `in-progress` with an empty worktree (0 dirty files, 0
commits ahead of dev). The next `drive`/`parent` run then calls
`_child_main_checkout_violation()` for that child, which finds
`_git_path_has_changes(wt)` false (correctly — no work) and therefore
attributes **pre-existing dirt in the main checkout and in other items'
sibling worktrees** to the failed child. The run fails closed with a long
'produced changes in the sibling worktree …' message naming paths the child
never touched.

## Impact during AH-0MWDC3L9I008INDP

Recovering child AH-0MWEXI5460080WEI required a manual `implement.py abort`
before the drive would proceed; the guard's message blamed
`src/test/playSceneBootGuard.test.ts` (main checkout) and files in
`wl-AH-0MTVYBL2L0085G6G`, `wl-AH-0MVAUU594007S92Q`,
`wl-AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA` and `/tmp/hw-base-check` — all other sessions' work.

## Acceptance criteria

- A driven child left `in-progress` by a **spawn failure** (no changes in its
  worktree, no commits ahead) is treated as startable-again/reset, not as a
  placement violation, so the next `drive` re-spawns it without manual
  `abort`.
- The placement guard distinguishes 'this child wrote elsewhere' from 'this
  child wrote nothing and other surfaces happen to be dirty' — the latter must
  not fail the chain.
- Regression test: a spawn-failed child plus a dirty main checkout and a dirty
  sibling worktree does not produce a `_child_main_checkout_violation`; a
  child that genuinely wrote only into a sibling worktree still does.
- No weakening of the genuine cross-worktree-write detection
  (SA-0MW5FIJNQ002Z24I).

## Key files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_child_main_checkout_violation`
  call sites in `phase_parent` (two sites: `skip-in-progress` path ~15158 and
  `implement` path ~15218)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` — existing
  sibling stray tests; add the spawn-fail regression

## Related

- SA-0MW5FIJNQ002Z24I — genuine cross-worktree-write detection; must not be
  weakened
- SA-0MVRN5Q67005H3M5 — behind-only child worktree mis-detected as 'has
  changes' and auto-finished (related verdict logic)
- AH-0MWFHLDAS008YG0P — original AI_Hell tracking item

## Plan (plan skill session on AH-0MWFHLDAS008YG0P)

Two children, implemented in dependency order (test-first):

1. **Test** — regression tests for spawn-failed child + dirty main/sibling
   not being a placement violation (6 ACs covering all four parent ACs).
2. **Fix** — code fix in `phase_parent`: check `worktree_verdict` before
   calling `_child_main_checkout_violation()`. Two call sites updated:
   `skip-in-progress` path (~15158) and `implement` path (~15218).

Dependency: Fix depends on Test (test-first ordering).

> Note: on 2026-11-14 the implementation could not be started because a Code
> Freeze was active (SorraAgents ship release in progress, run-release.js pid
> 2707644); the refusal was recorded as a comment on AH-0MWFHLDAS008YG0P.

## Impact

Driving an epic survives a child session that dies before it writes anything: the chain reports the child startable again and continues on the next run instead of stopping on unrelated dirt.
